newsitem.title: CHINA: France's Chirac sees bright future for China ties.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac sees bright future for China ties.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac launched the first day of a state visit to Beijing on Thursday with a rallying cry to make China a major partner for the 21st century and the signing of nearly $2.0 billion in contracts.

Crowning Chirac's first day in China was a $1.5 billion deal by Airbus Industrie -- reached only after tortuous talks that stretched into the early hours of Thursday -- to sell 10 A320 and 20 A321 planes to Chinese airlines.
"China must be one of our main partners," Chirac told French businessmen on the first day of his four-day visit.

"The China of tomorrow...will be one of the top nations of the world," he said. "I should like all my compatriots to share my conviction that despite the geographical distance between us, China must be one of our main partners."

President Jiang Zemin smiled broadly as he greeted Chirac at the Great Hall of the People, welcoming and praising the European head of state, who has taken a lead in playing down criticism of China's human rights record and opposing a western move this year to censure Beijing in the United Nations.
"On the subject of arms sales to Taiwan and human rights, China notes France has taken a wise decision," a spokesman quoted Jiang as saying in talks with his French counterpart.

Sino-French relations soured in the early 1990s over sales of French jet fighters and frigates to China's rival, Taiwan, but have recovered since Paris pledged in 1994 to end arms sales to the island that Beijing considers a rebel province.
The two leaders found plenty of common ground not just with a series of lucrative business deals but in their approach to the superpower position of the United States.
Chirac echoed one of Jiang's favourite themes with a call for a multi-polar world, one without a single superpower.
"The bi-polar world no longer exists and a multi-polar world is taking shape," state television quoted Chirac as telling Jiang. "We should promote this and strengthen ties."

France and Europe needed new ideas and a new approach in dealing with China, Chirac said, adding a call for China to become a political partner of France "in the multi-polar world we want to organise together".
That goal would be the major theme of a joint communique to be signed by Chirac and Jiang on Friday and which will state their desire and determination to strengthen ties.
However, business was the order of Chirac's first day.

Airbus Industrie signed a $1.5 billion deal to sell 30 planes to Chinese airlines and finalised a contract with Aviation Industries of China, Finmeccanica of Italy's Alenia, and Singapore Technologies Aerospace to manufacture a 100-seat jet. That project, to be in production by 2003, is expected to require investment of $2.0 billion.

Alenia, as part of an aircraft marketing consortium that also comprises Aerospatiale of France and British Aerospace Plc, signed an $80 million contract to sell five ATR-72 aircraft, with options on five more.

Rhone-Poulenc signed a 500 million franc joint venture to produce pesticide, Lafarge raised its stake in a cement joint venture by $75 million and China broke ground on the Ling'ao nuclear power plant near Hong Kong, for which Framatome is supplying the main nuclear reactors.
"For the first time in more than a century, China, which is no longer threatened on its borders, is enjoying exceptional stability and growth," Chirac said.
"France wishes to participate in this evolution. It is particularly well placed to do so," he said.
